ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the rhombus $ABCD$, $\angle C = 108^\circ$, the perpendicular bisector of $AD$ intersects the diagonal $BD$ at point $P$, and the foot of the perpendicular is $E$. Connecting $AP$, what is the measure of $\angle APB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given: Since $ABCD$ is a rhombus,\\
therefore $\angle C = \angle DAB = 108^\circ$, and $AD = AB$\\
therefore $\angle ADP = (180^\circ - 108^\circ) \div 2 = 36^\circ$,\\
since the perpendicular bisector of $AD$ intersects diagonal $BD$ at point $P$,\\
therefore $AP = DP$,\\
therefore $\angle ADP = \angle DAP = 36^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle APB = \angle ADP + \angle DAP = 36^\circ + 36^\circ = \boxed{72^\circ}$.

Also because the four sides of a rhombus are equal, AB = AD, triangle ABD is an isosceles triangle, and the vertex angle ∠DAB = 108°. Therefore the base angles ∠ADB = ∠ABD = (180° - 108°) / 2 = 36°. Because P is on BD, ∠ADP = ∠ADB = 36°. Also because P is on the perpendicular bisector of AD, PA = PD, triangle ADP is an isosceles triangle, therefore ∠DAP = ∠ADP = 36°. Since B, P, D are collinear, ∠APB is the exterior angle of triangle ADP at point P, so ∠APB = ∠ADP + ∠DAP = 36° + 36° = 72°.
